text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: `PD-98432` fired for service `inference-gateway-prod` — increased 5xx error rate (5m > 4%) in eu-west1. Trigger: http.5xx_rate > 4% (last 5m). Auto-page to primary oncall. See: https://pagerduty.redwood.example/incidents/PD-98432

mike-oncall: acked — I'm looking. any initial dashboard links?

anya: I'm on metrics. latency is fine, looks like a small subset of backend pods returning 502/503. traffic shifted to hostpool-b.

shawn: reproducing logs from gateway -> kv-cache timeouts and an increase in backend 502s. grabbing proxy logs.

leo: I can flip a quick fallback policy to the compat model (lower mem usage) if we need to reduce load on the failing replicas. we should check rollout status first.

mike-oncall: good call @leo. don't flip yet — want to confirm scope. what tenants affected?

emma-support: i've started a customer check-in list. initial scan of error reports shows 3 customers reporting degraded responses (chat/embedding API). I'll post customer IDs in a sec.

jordan-sre: runbook link — https://playbook.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx — step 1: check pod restarts / OOMs, step 2: identify model variants behind requests, step 3: consider draining problematic hosts.

shawn: quick dump from gateway (filtered):
```
[2026-03-14T02:18:12Z] gateway-1 eu-west1 -> backend-17 502 KV_CACHE_MISS timeout ms=1200
[2026-03-14T02:18:13Z] gateway-2 eu-west1 -> backend-18 502 WORKER_OOM? memory usage 96%
[2026-03-14T02:18:14Z] gateway-1 eu-west1 -> backend-17 502 KV_CACHE_MISS timeout ms=1100
```
looks like backend-17/18 are hot and failing.

mike-oncall: can we isolate by hostpool? shawn: which instances are in hostpool-b?

shawn: hostpool-b = backend-15..20. backend-17 has 42k requests in last 5m (normal ~8k). KV cache miss rate spiked.

anya: I'm rolling a cache warmup to hostpool-b with a targeted prefix cache preload (low risk). doing it now.

pagerduty-bot: PD-98432 acknowledged by mike-oncall at 02:19 UTC. Escalation timer paused.

mike-oncall: update — doing prefix cache preload and increasing max-connections to backend-17 temporarily. Jordan, any concerns about connection bump?

jordan-sre: connection bump ok for short window, watch CPU. set to revert in 10m if stable. also enable extra tracing on backend-17.

leo: preparing compat model fallback just in case. will not promote without explicit ok from oncall.

emma-support: pinged the three affected customers with a brief, non-technical note. CS ticket ids: CS-8221, CS-8228, CS-8229. I'll keep them updated.

shawn: cache preload started \u2014 rate shaping applied to avoid thundering herd. monitoring 5xx and token throughput.

mike-oncall: good. monitoring dashboards: 5xx dropped from 5.4% -> 1.3% in last 4m. still seeing sporadic errors from backend-18.

jordan-sre: backend-18 memory profile shows fragmentation + spike in ephemeral allocations for a specific model variant (gpt-large-quant). creating a short-lived alloc limit and moving traffic away in 2m.

shawn: diverted ~70% traffic from hostpool-b to hostpool-a for models with high mem. 5xx trending down.

mike-oncall: we're under threshold — PD will auto-resolve if stable for 10m, but let's keep watch for 20m. Emma, keep CS looped.

emma-support: noted, sending customers a heads-up that mitigation is in place and we'll follow up after stability window.

jordan-sre: follow-up actions assigned:
- cordon backend-18 and redeploy with latest memory-fix (jordan-sre)
- add early KV-cache warmup for hostpool-b on high-traffic model variants (anya)
- add alert refinement to only fire when >2 hostpools are showing >3% 5xx (mike-oncall)

mike-oncall: any postmortem required? severity: S2 (customer impact limited to small set, auto-mitigated). I'll open a short incident doc after the stability window.

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-98432 auto-resolved at 02:28 UTC (5xx rate back under threshold for 10m).

shawn: will follow up with logs + heap dump (if available) and post in the incident doc.

leo: leaving the compat fallback ready but not activated.

mike-oncall: thanks all — great quick work. I'll create the incident stub and assign owners for follow-ups. thumbs up :thumbsup:

emma-support: customers updated, monitoring ticket created.

jordan-sre: leaving notes in runbook and will push the tiny alert threshold change to staging for validation.

mike-oncall: closing thread once I publish the incident doc (will link here).
